last.verdict: Opendoor is buying homes far faster than it can sell them, and profit per home fell, leaving it deeper in debt.

takeaways.label: Margins missed
takeaways.text: Contribution margin, the profit on homes sold after direct costs, was 3.3%, below the 4%–4.5% guided and 5.8% last quarter. Profit per home fell to $12K from $22K.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt balloon
takeaways.text: Homes held rose to 7,596 from 5,459, and inventory value reached $2.6B from $925M at year-end. Most of it is funded by $2.4B of asset-backed debt. Cash is $910M.

takeaways.label: Weaker Q4 profit outlook
takeaways.text: Opendoor expects revenue up at least 40% year over year, but lower contribution profit and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70–85M, versus a $31M loss in Q3.

takeaways.label: Profit goal slipping
takeaways.text: Management admits it is "behind" its target of positive adjusted net income by the end of 2026. Adjusted net loss was $66M, and the net loss was $218M.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
